identity.title: High-Dimensional Prediction for Sequential Decision Making

problem.claim: Develop efficient multi-dimensional online forecasts for adversarial sequential decision settings, supporting many conditioning events that may depend on context and predictions.

gap.claim: The abstract identifies a lack of efficient algorithms for conditional regret under arbitrarily many intersecting context- and prediction-defined subsequences, and for online multicalibration at the stated ECE rate.

contributions.claim: An efficient forecasting algorithm achieving low bias under any polynomial number of context- and prediction-dependent conditioning events.
A prediction framework intended for polynomially many downstream decision makers with different utilities, with guaranteed diminishing swap regret at optimal rates.
Efficient algorithms for conditional regret in online combinatorial optimization and for online multicalibration with O(T^{2/3}) ECE rates.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe the conditional-regret and multicalibration algorithms as the first efficient algorithms with the corresponding scopes and rate.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that their forecasts have low bias for any polynomial number of conditioning events, including events depending on context and predictions.
The authors report guaranteed diminishing swap regret at optimal rates for any polynomial number of downstream decision makers with different utility functions.
The authors report an online multicalibration algorithm with O(T^{2/3}) rates in the ECE metric.

narrative_sequence.summary: Introduces an efficient algorithm for low-bias multi-dimensional forecasting under many adaptive conditioning events.
States that the forecasting algorithm is demonstrated through several applications.
Extends the predictions to multiple downstream decision makers and reports diminishing swap-regret guarantees at optimal rates.
Presents efficient conditional-regret algorithms for polynomially many intersecting subsequences defined by context and predictions.
Presents an efficient online multicalibration algorithm with an O(T^{2/3}) ECE rate.

source_observation.claim: The abstract states one forecasting capability and then instantiates it across downstream decision makers, combinatorial optimization, and calibration.

lessons.interpretation: A reusable abstraction is made more concrete by mapping it to distinct decision and evaluation objectives.
lessons.application: After introducing a general prediction primitive, organize the abstract around two or three explicit consequence domains and state the guarantee in each.
lessons.exception: This structure is unsuitable when applications are only speculative or lack a precise connection to the proposed primitive.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs each major algorithmic claim with a specific guarantee, including low bias, diminishing swap or conditional regret, and an O(T^{2/3}) ECE rate.

lessons.interpretation: Claim-to-metric alignment lets readers distinguish the paper's different success criteria.
lessons.application: For each contribution, name the evaluated or guaranteed metric and retain its scope and rate in the summary.
lessons.exception: Do not attach a metric when the source does not state one or when the condition needed to interpret it is missing.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact algorithmic construction, definitions of bias, regret, or ECE, or the meaning of “optimal rates.”
It does not provide experimental settings, baselines, numerical application results, or proof details.
The conditional-regret and multicalibration “first” claims are author-reported and not independently verified here.
